name: Marine Blue
lede: Marine Blue is a dark, slightly greenish blue of the sea; the one dictionary that defines it ties it to a military uniform.

sections.title: A uniform and the sea
sections.body: For Paterson, marine blue is a dark blue worn by the Royal Marines on their uniform [1]. That is a naval-and-military sense more than a color of the water, though the two meanings overlap, and the books read do not settle which came first [1].

sections.title: On the charts
sections.body: The library finds the color in Ridgway's 1912 atlas (plates VIII and XX), the 1955 ISCC-NBS blocks 173 and 179, and the xkcd survey, whose own marine blue is a much darker #01386A [2]. A near-duplicate is Dusky Greenish Blue, and Maerz and Paul's Peacock, first recorded in 1598, sits close by [2]. The nearest everyday name is [[denim]]; family names are [[navy]] and [[prussian-blue]] [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch is in 110 of 23,781 museum paintings, about 0.46 per cent [3]. It peaks in the 1900s at 0.9 per cent of paintings, 3.7 times the expected rate for the same museums [3]. Inside a painting it is most often an accent, in 31 per cent of the 52 paintings measured [3].
